Designing Resilient Ingestion Pipelines

Every ingestion system eventually meets the same three failures: the source is gone, the source is angry, and the source is lying. Treating those as one failure is how pipelines rot. A ledger that records the difference between a 403 challenge and a dead domain is the difference between a system that heals itself and one that silently loses content forever.

The trick is to keep classification in exactly one place. When seven fetchers each decide what a timeout means, you have seven opinions and six bugs. Centralize the mapping, test it once, and route every driver through it. The full argument is laid out in the ledger-driven design note and the companion piece on wayback fallbacks.

Politeness matters too: per-source delays serialize the pipeline, and that is fine. Synchronous code you can read beats asynchronous code you can debug. The queue is a file, the state is a log, and every decision leaves a line you can grep six months later when someone asks why a page was never fetched.
